items.title: Wild’s Joel Eriksson Ek exits vs. Maple Leafs with injury
items.summary: Centre Joel Eriksson Ek exited Thursday’s game against the Toronto Maple Leafs after suffering what appeared to be a head injury.
items.body: The Minnesota Wild will be hoping for the best for one of their alternate captains. Centre Joel Eriksson Ek exited Thursday's game against the Toronto Maple Leafs after suffering what appeared to be a head injury. The injury occurred midway through the second period. Eriksson Ek collided with Maple Leafs defenceman Jake McCabe near centre-ice, and the blueliner's shoulder made contact with his head. Eriksson Ek stayed down on the ice for some time before the officials whistled the play dead and the Wild medical staff were able to help him off the ice and into the locker room. Up to that point in the game, Eriksson Ek had played 10:52 while recording three shots on goal and two hits. Heading into Thursday's showdown, the 29-year-old had six goals and 11 assists in 20 games while playing 19:48 of ice time a night.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Winnipeg’s Cole Perfetti preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Kyle Connor’s goal . According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 3:32 (16:28 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Blue Jackets’ Rick Bowness misses game with illness
items.summary: Assistant coach Don Granato will take over the lead role of the Blue Jackets’ bench in Bowness’ absence.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Columbus Blue Jackets were without their head coach for Thursday’s game against the Tampa Bay Lightning , as Rick Bowness missed the match due to an illness. Bowness had missed the team’s morning skate earlier on Thursday, with the Blue Jackets confirmed that it was due to an illness. His status wasn’t confirmed for the game, but the team announced a half hour before puck drop that he would miss the game. With Bowness absent, assistant coach Don Granato assumed the lead role on the staff. Granato has some experience as a head coach, as he was the bench boss for four seasons with the Buffalo Sabres from 2021 to 2024. In 274 games with the Sabres, he had a 122-125-27 record, with the team failing to make the playoffs in all four seasons of his tenure. The Blue Jackets are certainly used to having a new face leading the coaching staff, as Bowness has been the team’s fifth head coach in just over three years, with Brad Larsen, Mike Babcock, Pascal Vincent and Dean Evason also working in the role in that time. In the team’s first 20 seasons prior to Larsen’s hiring in 2021, they had only had seven head coaches in franchise history. Bowness is in his second season (and first full season) with the Blue Jackets after he was hired on January 12th, 2026. In his 53 games with the team, they have a 28-20-5 record, with their .575 points percentage ranking 17th in the league in that span. At 71 years old, Bowness is the oldest head coach in the NHL. He hold the distinction of being the only head coach to operate behind the bench in five different decades, with his first season coming in 1988-89 with the original Winnipeg Jets. items.title: Lightning’s Anthony Cirelli, Erik Cernak out vs. Blue Jackets
items.summary: Cirelli has five goals and nine assists in 18 games this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images The Tampa Bay Lightning will be down a couple of key pieces for Thursday’s road game against the Columbus Blue Jackets . Speaking before Thursday’s game, Lightning head coach Jon Cooper revealed that forward Anthony Cirelli and defenseman Erik Cernak will not play against the Blue Jackets. Cirelli, 29, is out with an undisclosed injury, and it’s unclear how or when he picked up the injury. The Etobicoke, Ontario native has played all 18 of Tampa Bay’s games coming into Thursday, putting up five goals and nine assists for 14 points . Selected by the Lightning in the third round of the 2015 NHL Entry Draft, Cirelli is in his ninth full-time NHL season, having won the Stanley Cup in 2020 and 2021. He’s long been one of the most reliable defensive centers in the league, and is now in the fourth season of an eight-year, $50 million contract . Cernak, 29, is considered day-to-day. While Tampa Bay has not specified his injury, he likely suffered it during Wednesday’s 8-3 win over the Buffalo Sabres when he was checked awkwardly into the curved glass near the Lightning bench by Sabres forward Beck Malenstyn. Cernak was able to leave the ice under his own power, and did not return to the game. The Slovakian national has no goals and seven assists in 17 games played this season, while averaging just over 18 minutes of ice time. Selected by the Los Angeles Kings in the second round of the 2015 NHL Entry Draft, Cernak was acquired by Tampa Bay in February of 2017 in the deal that sent goaltender Ben Bishop to Los Angeles. He is now in the fourth season of an eight-year, $41.6 million contract . Following Thursday’s game in Columbus, the Lightning will begin a six-game homestand against the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday.

During an appearance on NHL Network’s NHL Tonight with host Tony Luftman, the former Washington Capitals head coach recently shared his thoughts on the upcoming candidacy of several former NHLers, making it clear that he would love to see Backstrom receive hockey’s highest individual honor. “I, certainly, for me, would love to see Nick get in,” Boudreau said. “I’d love to see Ryan Getzlaf get in and Eric Staal – three guys that I’ve coached that are all on the potential list. And I mean, three of the greatest people you ever want to meet. “I think all three deserve it, as well as I think Rod Brind’Amour deserves it. If you look at his hockey career, let alone his coaching career, what he’s done, to me, there’s no reason that he shouldn’t be in. Next year should be the year.” Boudreau coached Backstrom with the Capitals for parts of five seasons from 2007-08 to 2011-12, the first five years of the Swedish pivot’s career. During those campaigns, Backstrom quickly established himself as one of the NHL’s premier playmakers, becoming a foundational piece of the Caps alongside Alex Ovechkin . Backstrom finished his NHL career with 1,033 points (271 goals, 762 assists) in 1,105 regular-season games, ending his stint with the Capitals as the franchise leader in assists and ranking second in points, only to Ovechkin. He also helped Washington win its first Stanley Cup in 2018, posting 23 points (5g, 18a) in 20 postseason games. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports Showtime is back in action in the Windy City. On Thursday, the Chicago Blackhawks activated forward Patrick Kane from injured reserve. With that, he’s expected to be in the lineup for that night’s game, as the Blackhawks are set to play host to the Buffalo Sabres . Kane’s return seemed imminent, as he has been practicing with the main group for the past couple of days. He has missed the past three games after suffering an upper-body injury last Monday against the Colorado Avalanche . He left the contest, which saw the Hawks lose to the Avs by a final score of 5-2, in the second period. He was later placed on IR . With Kane out, Chicago extended its losing streak, which is now up to six games. Kane has been one of the Hawks’ more productive players so far this season, though that isn’t saying much. General manager Bill Guerin made a coy comment Thursday when a radio host advised him not to trade Yurov. “Hey, look, I know there are reports out there that we have offered him up, but nobody knows what I’ve offered, except Detroit,” Guerin said on “The Chad Hartman Show” on WCCO radio in Minneapolis. Larkin asked the Red Wings for a trade after last season, left the team Oct. 29 and is suspended without pay. The 30-year-old is a six-time 30-goal-scorer in the fourth year of an eight-year, $69.9 million contract ($8.7 million average annual value) he signed with Detroit on March 1, 2023. Minnesota selected Yurov with the No. 24 pick of the 2022 NHL Draft. The 22-year-old forward has seven points (six goals, one assist) in 20 games entering the Wild’s game at the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday (7 p.m. ET; SN, MINNHL, Wild+). The Los Angeles Kings announced that forward Kevin Fiala is set to make his 2026-27 season debut on Thursday night, as the Kings host the New York Islanders . Fiala has been out of action since suffering a gruesome leg injury while representing Switzerland at the 2026 Winter Olympics. The injury led him to undergo surgery that knocked him out for the rest of the 2025-26 season. Fiala also missed training camp and the first month of the new campaign while recovering. The 30-year-old will be a welcome addition to the lineup, as the Kings have struggled through the first quarter of the year. Through 16 games, Los Angeles has scored just 45 goals, which ranks 30th in the NHL. They also have a goal differential of -10, tied for 24th in the league. Fiala has been one of the Kings’ top scoring threats since he joined the organization in 2022. After posting consecutive 70-point campaigns, he registered 60 points in 81 games during the 2024-25 season. He was on pace to reach 60 points again last year before the injury, as Fiala had notched 18 goals and 40 points in 56 games prior to the Olympic Break. In 707 regular-season games in the NHL, Fiala has posted 229 goals and 299 assists for 528 points, with another 30 points in 49 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. Fiala is in the fifth season of the six-year contract extension, which he signed in June 2022. The deal carries an AAV of $7.875 million and includes a modified no-trade clause. The Kings (5-9-2) have lost back-to-back games heading into Thursday, and sit seventh in the Pacific Division , nine points back of the Utah Mammoth for the last Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.

items.body: First-ever Finnish-born goalie to make Hockey Hall of Fame does honors CAR@SEA: Rinne joins Aho and Kakko for the ceremonial puck drop in Finland An adoring crowd in Helsinki welcomed Pekka Rinne with a rousing ovation just before he dropped the ceremonial puck at the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki on Thursday. Rinne, who became the first ever Finnish-born goalie inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame earlier this week, did the honors ahead of the game between the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken. He was inducted to the Hockey Hall on Monday as part of the Class of 2026 alongside NHL players Carey Price , Patrice Bergeron , Keith Tkachuk and women's player Cindy Curley. Longtime executive Brian Burke was inducted as a builder. Rinne, who hails from Kempele, was on hand to do the honors in Helsinki for the special event. Instead of the captains taking the honorary faceoff, a pair of Rinne's Finnish countrymen did the honors: Hurricanes forward Sebastian Aho , from Rauma and Kraken forward Kaapo Kakko , a native of Turku. Rinne played 15 NHL seasons and posted 369 career wins, tied for 22nd most in NHL history. He won the Vezina Trophy 2018 and the King Clancy Trophy in 2021. His 2.43 goals-against average is 20th best in League history and career .917 save percentage is 14th all-time.

items.title: Sedins unhappy with Canucks’ results, weighing options amid dismal season
items.body: Daniel and Henrik Sedin say they're not happy with the Vancouver Canucks ' results, but they believe in their coaching staff and players. The NHL team's co-presidents of hockey operations spoke to reporters on Thursday about the beleaguered club, which sits at the bottom of the league standings with a 3-16-1 record. The Canucks have lost six straight games and 16 of their last 17. Daniel Sedin says they're evaluating players every day but have yet to see the group put together a full, consistent effort over an entire game. His twin brother, Henrik Sedin, says Vancouver's front office is "looking at all players" to see what options are available for improving the team, but that the Canucks won't simply trade top talent away to get more draft picks because they need players who can produce on the ice and support up-and-coming athletes. The Sedins played their entire 17-season NHL careers in Vancouver and were appointed the team's co-presidents of hockey operations in May after the Canucks finished the 2025-26 season last in the league.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images Usually, when a player says that he wants to leave a team, he will sulk and trudge through games, or simply not play at all. It was just a couple of weeks ago that the Tampa Bay Lightning legend made a trade request, as he reportedly wouldn’t re-sign with the only team he has ever known. While the announcement sent shockwaves through the league, it did little to deter the 33-year-old’s play. In the six games since the news broke, Kucherov has been on fire, scoring five goals and 11 points across six games, including a hat trick against the Buffalo Sabres on Wednesday night. On Thursday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton break down Kucherov’s incredible play since it came out that he wanted out of town. Carter Hutton: It’s been a show of talent so far, and I think this is one of those where you kind of kick the hornet’s nest, this is what you’re going to get. He was pretty clear about how he felt the way that he was treated, and it wasn’t about the money; it was about the disrespect. I think that factor is, now, he is playing with that edge and that fire, and there’s different players are motivated in different ways, and you have to find ways to do it. I think that’s what we’re seeing right now from Kucherov, is the fact that he’s motivated to be the best possible player that he can be, and to show BriseBois and his team he’s not turning on them, he’s not checking out, he’s just going to use this as fuel. Right now is a great example of a team that went into Buffalo and just absolutely waxed them last night. That is a big win and a statement win for the Lightning.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis Joey Cullen is going to get asked a lot of questions about his family’s hockey history. That comes with the territory – just ask Tij Iginla or Caleb Malhotra. Cullen’s family tree is especially impressive. His father, Matt, is a three-time Stanley Cup champion. Joey’s brother, Wyatt, was a top-10 pick by the Nashville Predators last year, and he’s expected to center USA’s top line at the World Juniors. And that’s only scratching the surface; multiple other family members ended up making the NHL as well. The 16-year-old was one of the top recruits for the U-17 USA Hockey National Team Development Program last spring. Many scouts viewed him as the premier offensive threat in the country, with a strong chance of going in the top five in 2028. items.title: Sharks’ Celebrini fifth-youngest player in NHL history to reach 200 career points
items.summary: Sidney Crosby, Wayne Gretzky, Jimmy Carson and Mario Lemieux are the only players to hit the milestone at a younger age.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images Macklin Celebrini has found himself in rare air. During the San Jose Sharks ‘ 3-2 shootout loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday , Celebrini hit the 200-point milestone in his career, becoming the fifth-youngest player to reach that threshold. Celebrini achieved the feat midway through the third period of the game, when an offensive zone sequence saw Will Smith pass the puck across the zone to Michael Kesselring, who had previously pinched up on the breakout rush and was still deep in the zone. Kesselring immediately bumped the puck towards Celebrini in the high slot, who faked the first shot to trick the defense and goalie before firing home a goal to cut Pittsburgh’s 2-1 lead in half and giving him his 200th career point. Celebrini then followed it up with the primary assist on Mason Marchment’s game-tying goal with a bit over four minutes to go in the third period, giving him his 201st point. With his 200th point, Celebrini became the fifth-youngest player to reach the milestone, doing so at the age of 20 years and 151 days. He joins some elite players in the process, with the four players ahead of him being Mario Lemieux (20 years, 133 days), Jimmy Carson (20 years, 107 days), Wayne Gretzky (19 years, 347 days) and Sidney Crosby (19 years, 207 days). Admittedly, Celebrini and Crosby do have an advantage to get there in a similar amount of time to the likes of Gretzky and Lemieux, as the two have birthdays closer to the cut-off date for draft eligibility, with Celebrini’s being June 13th and Crosby’s being August 7th. items.body: EDMONTON — Back in 1987, when the Edmonton Oilers would win a Stanley Cup off a season in which their team save percentage was .881, Grant Fuhr taught us that there was only one stat that truly mattered. And it starts with a ‘W’. But the game changed along the way, and as the Oilers careened from Mikko Koskinen to Connor Ingram, from Mike Smith to Stuart Skinner, we realized that perhaps it was an environment issue in Edmonton as much as it was about the quality of the netminders. Tristan Jarry stopped 30 shots, Evan Bouchard scored the OT winner, and for the second straight game the visitors were the better team yet lost, as the Oilers beat the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2. “Good teams ... what they do is find ways to win,” said head coach Mike Babcock. “They rely on their structure even when it's a disaster. You're five tight (around the net) and doing good things. “Jars made tons of good saves, but he didn't have to go east-west a ton. There weren't lateral feeds ... the (shot attempts) were coming right at him. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Chicago Blackhawks have been arguably the biggest disappointment in the NHL this season, and general manager Kyle Davidson knows it. Granger’s update suggests the Golden Knights will activate Wotherspoon from the long-term injured reserve ahead of tonight’s contest against the Utah Mammoth. Vegas acquired Wotherspoon in a trade with the Pittsburgh Penguins this past offseason. The 29-year-old blueliner signed a two-year, $2MM contract with the Penguins a year before. The Golden Knights had to part with Kaedan Korczak , who recently signed a four-year, $13MM ($3.25MM AAV) extension, to acquire Wotherspoon. Still, since Pittsburgh ate 50% of Wotherspoon’s salary ($500K), Vegas eagerly made the swap. Unfortunately, because of his upper-body ailment, Wotherspoon’s hasn’t been able to build on last year’s success. In 80 games with the Penguins, Wotherspoon scored three goals and 30 points with a +17 rating, while averaging 20:10 of ice time per game. The Surrey, BC, native also blocked 112 shots and delivered 162 hits, making him a high-value two-way defenseman with his relatively low salary. The multi-week upper-body injury has limited him to six games with his new club. He’s gone scoreless in those six contests, with a -6 rating and a dismal 82.1% on-ice SV%. Still, if he stays healthy, Wotherspoon has 65 more regular-season contests to have a strong year heading into unrestricted free agency. items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney previously stated that Russians wouldn’t be playing in the upcoming tournament.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Canada is digging in its heels about allowing Russia to play in Alberta next month. According to TSN’s Gord Miller, the Canadian government has told both Hockey Canada and the International Ice Hockey Federation it will not issue visas to Russian players seeking to play in the upcoming IIHF World Junior Championship. Also, players who might already have visas – players in the Canadian Hockey League – are considered ineligible to participate, even if it was under a neutral flag. This comes not long after Canadian prime minister Mark Carney stated that Russia “will not” be at the World Juniors, which are set to begin on Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer. The whole debate on whether Russia would be allowed to play in the upcoming event came after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation must be allowed to compete in IIHF events, citing that the IIHF didn’t provide enough evidence to keep the ban on Russian teams in place. The IIHF, along with numerous international hockey federations, has voiced its displeasure on the decision. Nations have come forward, stating that they won’t play Russia in any international events, with some big-time sponsors threatening to pull their funding from the IIHF, if Russia is allowed to compete. As it stands, Norway, the last-ranked team heading into the WJC, has been informed that it will be removed from the tournament to make way for Russia . However, many expect Russia to be forced to back out, leading to Norway’s readmission to the event. The ban on Russian hockey teams dates back to 2022, when the nation invaded Ukraine shortly after the Beijing Olympics.

items.body: Nick Cousins won't be back on the ice for the next little while. The Ottawa Senators enforcer is out at least one week after absorbing a massive hit from Washington Capitals defenceman Jakob Chychrun on Tuesday, head coach Travis Green told reporters Wednesday. Cousins was briefly knocked out by the play, Green said. No penalty was called. Washington went on to win 3-2 in overtime. As Cousins looked to clear the puck out of the defensive end late in the third period, Chychrun caught him with his head down and sent him flying into the boards. Cousins stayed face-down on the ice before eventually getting to his feet and making his way off the ice with assistance from teammates. He did not return. "He's not doing great," Green said after the game, adding that Cousins did not go to the hospital. "I thought it was a head shot to a player who wasn't ready for it. They must have saw it different." The officials reviewed the hit for a five-minute major, but determined there was no penalty. "I should be careful what I say; I don't like seeing that stuff," Senators forward Ridly Greig said. Added captain Thomas Chabot: "I hate, I think everybody hates, these scenes in hockey, in any sport." Cousins, 33, has two goals and one assist in 19 games this season. He was 13 years old and found himself at Hartwall Arena -- the mecca of Finnish hockey and home to the Finnish national ice hockey team -- to watch the Carolina Hurricanes take on the Minnesota Wild in the 2010 NHL Premiere Series. items.title: Briere says Flyers have no plan to trade Michkov
items.summary: The message from Daniel Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Matvei Michkov.
items.body: TORONTO — Despite a report about Matvei Michkov’s apparent unhappiness and potential interest in a change of scenery, the Philadelphia Flyers say they have not received a request for a trade from Michkov’s agent and were surprised by the news. “This is all news to me,” Flyers general manager Daniel Briere said. Beyond that, the message from Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Michkov. “No, that’s not the plan at all,” Briere said. “We’ve never discussed that.” The report from NHL Network ’s Kevin Weekes cited “internal turmoil” with the Flyers as part of Michkov’s interest in “wanting a new start elsewhere,” but earlier on Wednesday following the GM Meetings in downtown Toronto, Briere took zero issue with Michkov’s emotion that spilled over to the bench during an in-game confrontation with teammate Nick Seeler. “I actually like the fact that our guys are fiery and they want to win,” Briere said. “That’s what I saw [in Vancouver]. It’s showing competitive players. That’s what we’re looking for, that’s what we want. The reality is, the team hasn’t performed great this year and players expect more out of themselves.” Briere scoffed at the notion that the in-game quarrelling over a sequence in the offensive zone had any indication that the Flyers were lacking in the culture department, as some observers have suggested. “If we had a culture where guys are yelling at each other and no one is responding, a culture that guys don’t care about winning, then we’d be in trouble,” Briere said. “But when you show a culture that guys want to better themselves and they’re not happy where they are, I expect that.” One of the most emotional and competitive players on the last great Flyers teams, Briere said he was glad there weren’t as many cameras as there are now.

She has helped Finland reach incredible heights over the last two decades, and has been a leader for Finnish hockey ever since she was named team captain prior to the 2012 World Championship.
